# CKW Elements - AI Agent Guide

CKW Elements is a token-first React design system. Build UI by importing tokens, icons, and components from the packages instead of copying styles from Storybook.

## Install

```bash
npm install @ckwag/elements-tokens @ckwag/elements-icons @ckwag/elements
```

Peer dependencies: `react` and `react-dom` 18 or 19.

## Required App Setup

Import token CSS once in the app entry point:

```css
@import '@ckwag/elements-tokens/tokens.css';
```

React applications can import components from either the package root or the explicit React subpath:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Button, InputField, Select } from '@ckwag/elements';
```

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Button, InputField, Select } from '@ckwag/elements/react';
```

If a bundler does not process CSS side-effect imports from packages, import the aggregate component CSS explicitly after the tokens:

```css
@import '@ckwag/elements-tokens/tokens.css';
@import '@ckwag/elements/styles.css';
```

Apps that use cascade layers can use the layered CSS exports:

```css
@layer ckw-tokens, ckw-elements, app;
@import '@ckwag/elements-tokens/tokens.layered.css';
@import '@ckwag/elements/styles.layered.css';
```

## Token Assets

These files are published with the deployed documentation for agents and build tooling:

- `tokens/tokens.css`: CSS custom properties and typography utility classes.
- `tokens/tokens.layered.css`: the same CSS wrapped in `@layer ckw-tokens`.
- `tokens/tokens.js`: JavaScript named exports and a default token map.
- `tokens/tokens.d.ts`: TypeScript declarations for JavaScript token exports.
- `tokens/tokens.json`: DTCG token source.

The npm token package also exports:

```ts
import tokens, { interactivePrimary, spacingM } from '@ckwag/elements-tokens';
import '@ckwag/elements-tokens/tokens.css';
import rawTokens from '@ckwag/elements-tokens/tokens.json';
```

## Styling Rules

- Use only semantic tokens for component colors: `--text-primary`, `--background-default`, `--interactive-primary`, `--border-soft`.
- Do not use primitive color tokens in product components: avoid `--color-green-600`, `--color-grey-800`, and similar primitives.
- Never hardcode hex colors in repository UI code except Storybook theme configuration where Storybook requires raw colors.
- Use CKW green for primary actions. Do not substitute blue as the primary brand color.
- Use `font-family: var(--font-family-brand), sans-serif`.
- Prefer token spacing, radii, shadows, border weights, and typography variables over raw CSS values.

## Component APIs

All prop values are lowercase in code. Figma shows the same values in Title Case (`Variant=Primary` maps to `variant="primary"`). Components forward native HTML attributes where noted.

### Button

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" size="large" onClick={save}>
  Save
</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" href="/help" target="_blank">
  Help
</Button>
```

- `variant`: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `tertiary`
- `size`: `large` (default), `medium`, `small`
- `fullWidth`: boolean
- `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`: React node
- `loading`: boolean; shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, and blocks interaction
- `href`, `target`, `rel`: render as a link with button styling; `rel` defaults to `noopener noreferrer` for `target="_blank"`
- `type`: native button type, defaults to `button`
- Accepts native `<button>` props and forwards its ref

### Badge

```tsx
<Badge status="success" showIcon>
  Aktiv
</Badge>
```

- `status`: `neutral` (default), `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `brand`
- `size`: `medium` (default), `small`
- `showIcon`: boolean; `info`, `success`, `warning`, and `error` have a default icon
- `icon`: React node; required for `neutral` and `brand` when `showIcon` is true
- `children`: short label; the meaning must always be in the text
- Accepts native `<span>` props

### InputField

```tsx
<InputField label="Name" placeholder="Enter name" errorText={error} />
<InputField label="Amount" prefix="CHF" suffix=".00" description="Without VAT" />
```

- `label`, `placeholder`: string
- `description`: help text below the input
- `errorText`: non-empty string triggers the error state
- `optional`: shows "(optional)" next to the label
- `prefix`, `suffix`: short text inside the field, e.g. currency or unit
- `icon`: trailing React node
- `showInfo`, `onInfoClick`: info button next to the label
- `type`: native input type, defaults to `text`
- `id`: auto-generated when omitted and wired to the label
- Accepts native `<input>` props (`value`, `onChange`, `disabled`, `name`, `required`, ...) and forwards its ref

### PasswordInput

```tsx
<PasswordInput label="Password" name="password" required autoComplete="current-password" />
```

- Inherits InputField props except `type` and `icon`
- `visible`: controlled visibility state
- `defaultVisible`: initial uncontrolled visibility state
- `onVisibilityChange`: `(visible: boolean) => void`
- `visibilityToggleButtonProps`: native toggle button props

### Select

```tsx
<Select
  label="Country"
  placeholder="Choose a country"
  options={[
    { value: 'ch', label: 'Switzerland' },
    { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' },
  ]}
  value={country}
  onValueChange={setCountry}
/>
```

- `label`: string (required)
- `options`: array of `{ value, label, disabled }`; `value` must not be an empty string (see KNOWN_ISSUES.md)
- `value` / `defaultValue`: controlled or uncontrolled selection
- `onValueChange`: `(value: string) => void`
- `placeholder`, `description`, `errorText`, `optional`, `showInfo`, `onInfoClick`
- `disabled`, `required`, `name` (renders a hidden native select for form submission), `id`
- `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`: list open state
- Built on `@radix-ui/react-select`; forwards its ref to the trigger button

### InlineMessage

```tsx
<InlineMessage status="info" title="Statusmeldung">
  Hier steht eine kurze Erklaerung zum aktuellen Status oder zur naechsten Aktion.
</InlineMessage>
```

- `status`: `info` (default), `success`, `warning`, `error`
- `title`: React node
- `children`: React node
- `icon`: React node; defaults to the status icon
- `showIcon`: boolean, defaults to true
- `breakpoint`: `auto` (default), `desktop`, `mobile`
- `role`: defaults to `note`

### SegmentedControl

```tsx
<SegmentedControl
  aria-label="View"
  segments={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
  ]}
  activeValue="list"
  onChange={setView}
/>
```

- `segments`: array of `{ value, label, icon }`, minimum 2
- `activeValue`: string
- `onChange`: `(value: string) => void`
- `variant`: `default` (auto width), `fill` (equal width)
- `contentMode`: `label` (default), `icon-label`, `icon-compact`
- `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: accessible name for the radio group

### LoadingSpinner

```tsx
<LoadingSpinner size={20} />
```

- `size`: number in pixels, defaults to 20
- `className`: string

## Icons

`@ckwag/elements-icons` exports one React component per icon plus a name-based `Icon` component:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Icon, IconSearch, iconNames } from '@ckwag/elements-icons';

<IconSearch />
<IconSearch title="Search" size={16} />
<Icon name="search" />
```

- Component names are `Icon` + PascalCase icon name (`chevron-down` is `IconChevronDown`).
- `size`: number or string, defaults to 24.
- `title`: accessible label. Omit it for decorative icons, which render `aria-hidden`.
- Icons use `currentColor`; set color with a semantic token on the parent.
- `iconNames` and `iconMetadata` list all available icons.

## Agent Skills

Use these deployed prompt files when an AI agent needs CKW-specific behavior:

- `skills/ckw-prototyping.md`: use for rapid UI prototyping.
- `skills/ckw-components.md`: use for reusable React components.

## Storybook Fetch Notes

Storybook builds to static files. It is not server-side rendered HTML per route. Agents should fetch these plain-text/static assets first:

- `llms.txt`
- `llms-full.txt`
- `DESIGN.md`
- `tokens/tokens.css`
- `tokens/tokens.json`
- `skills/ckw-prototyping.md`
- `skills/ckw-components.md`

For story metadata, fetch Storybook's generated `index.json` from the deployed build.

Use Storybook URLs for visual inspection and the static assets above for code generation context.
